questions.question_text:
A quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal, and none of its angles is a right angle.
Give the most specific name guaranteed by the given information.

options.why: Ignores the statement that none of the angles is a right angle.
A parallelogram is a kind of trapezium under the definition used here, but parallelogram is the more specific name.
Equal opposite pairs do not guarantee equal adjacent pairs. A kite is not guaranteed.

questions.solution_text:
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel and equal, which guarantees a parallelogram.
Parallelogram.
All four sides equal is not given, so a rhombus is not guaranteed.

questions.question_text:
All four sides of a quadrilateral are equal, and none of its angles is a right angle.
Give the most specific name guaranteed by the given information.

options.why: Assumes four equal sides forces right angles, ignoring the stated condition.
A rhombus also fits the kite definition, but rhombus is the more specific name for four equal sides.
A rhombus also fits the trapezium definition, but trapezium is a less specific name.

questions.solution_text:
Four equal sides give a rhombus. The stated lack of right angles rules out a square.
Rhombus.

questions.question_text:
A quadrilateral has consecutive side lengths $7\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$.
Which is the most specific name guaranteed by this information?

options.why: Treats the equal adjacent pairs as equal opposite pairs; each pair of opposite sides has lengths $7\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$.
Treats two equal pairs as four equal sides, ignoring that $7\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ are different lengths.
Assumes right angles without any given and ignores the unequal opposite sides.

questions.solution_text:
The two sides of length $7\text{ cm}$ meet at one corner, and the two sides of length $12\text{ cm}$ meet at another.
There are two pairs of equal adjacent sides.
Kite.

questions.question_text:
A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides, of lengths $8\text{ cm}$ and $13\text{ cm}$.
Which is its most specific classification?

options.why: Treats one parallel pair as two parallel pairs and ignores that the parallel opposite sides have unequal lengths.
Assumes four right angles; a rectangle would also need two parallel pairs and equal opposite sides.
Assumes four equal sides despite the given unequal lengths and ignores that a rhombus has two parallel pairs.

questions.solution_text:
Exactly one pair of opposite sides is parallel, so the quadrilateral is a trapezium.
Trapezium.

questions.question_text:
Consider these statements.
Statement 1: Every rhombus is a parallelogram.
Statement 2: Every parallelogram is a rhombus.
Which statements are always true?

options.why: Reverses the hierarchy: a rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, but a parallelogram need not have four equal sides.
Assumes every parallelogram has four equal sides, confusing equal opposite sides with all sides equal.
Fails to recognise that every rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel and is therefore a parallelogram.

questions.solution_text:
Statement 1 is always true: a rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so it is a parallelogram.
Statement 2 is not always true: a parallelogram need not have four equal sides.
Only statement 1.
